standard.title: Specification for Packing Paper, Water Proof, Bitumen-Laminated (Second Revision)

sectional_committee.name: Paper Based Packaging Materials Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for water-proof, bitumen-laminated packing paper utilized for wrapping, bale-lining, and protective packaging of diverse industrial and consumer goods.
standard.scope: This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for water-proof, bitumen-laminated packing paper utilized for wrapping, bale-lining, and protective packaging of diverse industrial and consumer goods.

amendments.summary: Amendment No. 1 (August 2004) is active on this copy.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) as a certified assurance of waterproof barrier quality. Compliance with IS 1398 is widely integrated into defense packaging, seaworthy textile bales, export shipping specifications, and civil construction (such as under-layment beneath concrete linings to prevent moisture loss).
requirements: Specifies Type 1 packing paper as a water-proof, bitumen-laminated kraft paper combination designed for high barrier performance in general packaging.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (August 2004), the wording on Page 4, clause 2.1, line 5 is amended to substitute 'kraft paper' in place of the typographical error 'draft paper'.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (August 2004), the packaging requirements on Page 5, clause 3.4, line 1 are amended to substitute 'length of minimum 100 metres' in place of 'length of 100 metres'.

The laminate must utilize a continuous, uniform interlayer of food-grade or packing-grade bitumen to bond the paper plies. It must present no delamination, bare patches, or bleeding under normal storage temperatures.
The paper must withstand water penetration tests, ensuring that no liquid water seeps through the bitumen barrier when tested under a standard hydrostatic or surface-contact time-exposure head.
Observed or calculated values during testing must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained must match the specified limit.
